claims.text: POL-NS-02 makes arrival an arithmetic question, and the arithmetic fails for the driver. The STANDARD-zone arrival radius is 50 m and the proximity test admits only fixes reporting horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better. Not one of the eight fixes in the driver's trace carries an accuracy figure, so under POL-NS-02 every one of them is ignored for this test and counts as evidence of neither presence nor absence. The derived arrival block records qualifying_fix_count = 0, rider_qualifying_fix_count = 0 and longest_qualifying_run.fix_count = 0 across the whole trace. POL-NS-02 states in terms that where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. The trace is impaired at weight 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, and I disclose that impairment; it only weakens the trace as proof of arrival and cannot supply the arrival the driver needs, because the driver bears the burden of all four conjunctive limbs of POL-NS-01 and has not carried limb (b).

Independently of arrival, the waiting period the fee is meant to purchase never happened. The STANDARD minimum dwell is 300 seconds. The derived arrival block records longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec = 0.0, accumulated_dwell.longest_run_sec = 0.0 and accumulated_dwell.run_count = 0, against a shortfall_sec of 300.0. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full on a shortfall, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, so limb (c) of POL-NS-01 fails. And because no qualifying dwell ever elapsed, the 08:51 termination cannot satisfy limb (d) either: that limb requires the trip to end at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, and there was no such moment. These figures come from the impaired trace (weight 0.6; LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD), which I disclose; a record whose sampling gaps run to 240 seconds cannot be read as a continuous five-minute hold.

The driver cannot repair the shortfall by accumulating separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i). That limb requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose active window covers the waiting period, carrying a type of KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00901-01, is MISSING: weight 0.0 and no payload. Limb (i) is therefore unavailable and no interval may be summed. The absence is itself citable — there is no advisory on this record that could have made holding position at the pin lawfully impossible — and the 300-second minimum stands unadjusted.

The GPS trace is impaired for policy purposes, not merely tagged. Five of the seven inter-fix intervals exceed POL-NS-08(b)'s 120-second gap limb (180, 240, 180, 180 and 180 seconds), the waiting window from the 08:43 arrival marker to the 08:51 cancellation holds only four fixes where that limb requires six, and the trace omits the rider_track entirely. Each of those is limb (b) on its own. The trace's weight is 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, and I disclose that any claim of mine resting on it is down-weighted; the consequence for this case is that no uninterrupted 300-second in-geofence hold can be evidenced at all, so the fee has nothing behind it.

The ledger does not reconcile with the policy that fixes the amount. POL-NS-01 fixes the chargeable fee at the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), which is $4.00, and POL-NS-08(d) makes a mismatch between fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee and that figure a fare defect. The ledger charges $5.00, a difference of $1.00. The artifact is impaired at weight 0.75 with issue code PARTIAL_RECORD, which I disclose. Whatever else is decided, no ruling can leave the rider paying $1.00 more than the schedule authorises, and this defect is independent of the GPS dispute — it is a defect on the platform's own ledger line.

The facts that decide this dispute — the driver's arrival and his dwell — are carried by a single carrier. The trip_record's 08:43 marker was auto-confirmed from the same GPS measurement, so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and the trace are one artifact and not two, and no independent artifact corroborates either fact. POL-GEN-02 caps confidence at the weight of the artifact carrying the deciding fact, which here is 0.6, below the 0.70 floor. On this record the pipeline cannot sustain a charge against the rider, and to the extent the judge finds the deciding fact rests solely on impaired evidence, POL-NS-09(a) and (e) require the case to escalate with the disputed $5.00 held rather than collected — which at the very least means the rider does not fund a charge the record cannot support.

claims.text: POL-NS-04 is the rider's principal route to a no-fault refund on coordination grounds, and its limb (a) fails outright. Limb (a) requires at least one message from the RIDER during the waiting window whose content is locating or coordinating — their own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that they cannot see the vehicle. The chat log runs from 08:43:00 to 08:51:00 and holds six entries; every one is from the DRIVER or the SYSTEM. The rider never asked where the car was, never named an entrance or bay, and never said they could not find the vehicle. Limb (a) is not met, so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider.

Even if limb (a) were somehow met, POL-NS-04 limb (b) is affirmatively failed. The clause requires that the driver NEITHER replied in the chat within 120 seconds of the rider's message NOR placed an in-app voice call before terminating. The driver did both. He posted messages at 08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30 and 08:50:45, and the trip record carries in-app call CALL-00901-001, initiated by the DRIVER at 08:47:05 and unanswered after 22 seconds. On either limb the rider-exonerating clause does not apply and no refund flows from it.

POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are satisfied on the platform's own records. Limb (a): the trip record contains a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 08:43:00, auto-confirmed from a GPS measurement. Limb (d): there is no boarding event, the trip status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER, and it terminated at 08:51:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. The rider-displacing clauses POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 do not fire (argued below), so the fee stands as itemised.

The dwell limb is corroborated by a clean artifact independent of the GPS. The chat log, at weight 1.0, shows the driver present and waiting from his 08:43:00 message — 'I've arrived at the pickup point, I'm at the lobby area' — through his 08:50:45 message — 'Please let me know, otherwise I'll have to cancel the trip' — with intermediate messages at 08:45:20 and 08:49:30 identifying the vehicle (white Honda HR-V, SGP 4521 M). That is 480 seconds of continuous presence at the pickup, comfortably above the 300-second STANDARD minimum, closing only when the SYSTEM logs the cancellation at 08:51:00.

I disclose that the GPS trace on which the rider's arithmetic must rest is IMPAIRED: issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, weight_multiplier 0.6. Five of its seven inter-fix intervals (180, 240, 180, 120, 120, 180, 180 seconds) exceed POL-NS-08(b)'s 120-second gap limb, the waiting window holds only four fixes against the six that limb requires, and no rider track was supplied. Under POL-GEN-02(1) that impairment must be stated in the same claim that cites it, and under POL-NS-08 a claim resting on this artifact is down-weighted: it cannot alone support a ruling against the driver.

The rider's cleanest arithmetic route is POL-NS-02, but the clause cannot carry it here. POL-NS-02's own drafting note states that a trace too sparse to establish three consecutive in-radius readings is 'impaired under POL-NS-08(b) rather than proof of absence'. This trace is exactly that shape — four fixes inside the waiting window, with no accuracy data. The absence of a qualifying in-radius fix is an impairment of the record, not a demonstration that the driver never arrived, and the clause's stated consequence (limb (b) fails, full refund) does not attach to a trace the clause itself classifies as impaired. (The trace is impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

POL-NS-02 admits only fixes whose reported horizontal accuracy is 25 m or better, and not one fix in this trace reports any accuracy field at all. The derived qualifying_fix_count of 0 therefore measures the trace's missing data, not the driver's conduct: on its own terms the clause's proximity test cannot be run, and the policy itself says such fixes 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence'. The zero dwell figure cannot be turned into an affirmative finding against the fee. (The trace is impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

POL-NS-05 sets aside an arrival marker only where the trace places the driver more than 300 m from the pin at the marker, or shows him travelling at 15 km/h or above. Neither is established here. The pre-pass records no clock skew — the 08:43:00 marker is the nearest fix timestamp to the second, so POL-NS-08(a) is not engaged — and the driver's own track records a minimum distance to the pickup pin of 0 m across its fixes, with a mean of 274 m and a maximum of 1,109 m, the profile of a vehicle that drove up to the pin and held there. The marker is not false on this record and the waiting clock runs from it. (That derived minimum is drawn from the impaired trace: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

POL-NS-06 refunds a rider only where the effective in-geofence dwell, computed under POL-NS-02, falls short of the minimum for the zone class. No such dwell is computable here, because no fix carries the accuracy POL-NS-02 requires, so the clause's premise cannot be established on this record. Its accumulation limb (i) is expressly unavailable as well: EV-ADVIS-00901-01, the traffic advisory, is MISSING, and limb (i) requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated. A MISSING artifact keeps its identifier, carries weight 0.0, and can carry no fact; it cannot be asserted against, and it exonerates no one. The shortfall arithmetic therefore proves nothing against the fee. (The GPS trace is impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

The rider's account — that they were at the lobby and the driver was not — has no location evidence behind it at all. The trace carries no rider track (rider_fix_count 0), and under POL-NS-04 limb (c) an absent rider track is expressly neutral: the rider-presence test cannot be run and must be recorded as unrun rather than inferred either way. The only record of the rider's whereabouts is the claim text itself. The driver's whereabouts, by contrast, are carried by the platform's own auto-arrival marker and by six timed chat entries over an eight-minute window. (The trace is impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

If the fee is found chargeable, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's compensation at 80 percent of the itemised cancellation fee, and the anti-farming bar cannot trip. That bar withholds compensation only where driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 4 or more AND exceeds 0.08 of driver_profile.completed_trips_30d; the field is null on this record, which is not '4 or more'. POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter for the trailing-30-day figure this clause names, so the check does not engage and compensation is payable — the derived money block computes the driver compensation at SGD 4.00. I disclose that the fare ledger supporting the amount is impaired (PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.75).

If the Judge concludes the record cannot settle arrival and dwell, the disposition that protects the fee is escalation, not refund. The trip record's auto-arrival marker and the GPS trace's zero qualifying fixes contradict each other directly on arrival and on dwell, and no clause resolves that conflict because the trace is accuracy-blind — POL-NS-09(b). In the alternative, the sole evidence for the deciding dwell fact is the trace, impaired under POL-NS-08(b), which caps the ruling at PARTIAL_REFUND and sends the case to the human reviewer under POL-NS-09. On either path the disputed fee is held rather than refunded while review is pending. (The trace is impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

I disclose a further defect rather than leave it to my opponent: the fare ledger is IMPAIRED — issue code PARTIAL_RECORD, weight_multiplier 0.75 — and its SGD 5.00 cancellation line does not reconcile with the fee schedule, which yields SGD 4.00 as the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00). That mismatch engages POL-NS-08(d). It is a defect in the amount recorded, not in the chargeability of the fee: it cannot convert a legitimate no-show charge into the full reversal the rider seeks.

ruling.explanation:
RIDER — your $5.00 no-show charge is not being refunded today, and it is not being upheld either: the case goes to a human reviewer with the money held. DRIVER — no compensation is payable on this record. Both of you are reading the same broken instrument, and it settles nothing.

The charge can only stand if the driver carries all four limbs of POL-NS-01. He carries limb (a) — trip record TRIP-2026-09945 has an 08:43:00 arrival marker — and the reason-code half of limb (d) (cancelled by the driver at 08:51:00 on RIDER_NO_SHOW). Limbs (b) and (c) both run on the GPS trace EV-GPS-00901, and that trace cannot be read. Not one of its fixes carries a reported horizontal accuracy, so under POL-NS-02 every fix is evidence of neither presence nor absence and none establishes arrival; the derived qualifying_fix_count is 0. The trace is impaired for policy under POL-NS-08(b): gaps of 180 s, 240 s and 180 s inside the waiting window exceed the 120 s limb, the window 08:43–08:51 holds four fixes against the six required, and no rider track was supplied. Its weight is 0.6 (LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD).

That impairment decides the case. The arrival and dwell facts are carried by the GPS trace alone. The trip record's 08:43:00 marker was auto-confirmed from the same GPS measurement, so it is one carrier, not two. The chat log EV-CHAT-00901 (weight 1.0) does not carry the fact: POL-NS-01(c) measures dwell from qualifying in-geofence GPS fixes, and the driver's own messages record only that he sent them — the clause reads the trace, not the log, and POL-NS-03 reads the chat log only to allocate fault. Where the test admitted no reading at all, an account offered in its place stands in for the test and neither lifts the cap nor stops the impaired trace being the only evidence. Limbs (b) and (c) are therefore undecided, not failed: an undecided limb supports neither the charge nor a refund on those grounds.

So POL-NS-08's closing sentence and POL-NS-09(e) apply: the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under the clause's own limbs, the case escalates, and the $5.00 is held rather than collected or refunded. The same result follows from POL-NS-09(a), because the confidence this record supports is capped at the trace's 0.6, below the 0.70 floor.

On the specific arguments. RIDER, your claims that POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 give you a full refund are rejected as affirmative grounds — the zero dwell and zero qualifying fixes measure the trace's missing accuracy data, not the driver's conduct, and POL-NS-02's own drafting note calls a trace too sparse to raise three in-radius readings impaired rather than proof of absence. DRIVER, your POL-NS-04 arguments are accepted (the rider sent no locating message during the window, and you both replied in chat and placed the 08:47:05 in-app call), so that clause does not exonerate the rider; your POL-NS-05 point is accepted (the trace's minimum distance to the pin is 0 m, so the marker is not false and no false-arrival referral arises); your chat-log dwell claim is rejected for the reason above; and POL-NS-07 compensation is not reached, because it presupposes a chargeable fee and the fee is not established — and escalation displaces it in any event. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is null on this record, and prior_no_show_flags was rightly not substituted for it.

Both sides disclosed the ledger defect, and it is real: the fare breakdown charged $5.00 while fee_schedule yields $4.00 as the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00) — a $1.00 difference, a POL-NS-08(d) defect. Because escalation is terminal and holds the whole fee, I do not dispose of it here. Whether the $5.00 should be reconciled to $4.00, and whether the driver in fact arrived at Tiong Bahru Plaza and held the 300-second STANDARD minimum between 08:43 and 08:51, are the questions the reviewer must settle. The escalation packet — both briefs, the admissibility pre-pass report, every clause relied on and this reasoning — goes to human review. No referral is added: no clause on these facts produces one.

To the rider and the driver: I cannot decide this dispute on the present record, so I am escalating it to a human reviewer. ESCALATE is terminal — no refund and no charge issues now, and the contested $5.00 no-show cancellation fee is held rather than collected or refunded while review is pending.

WHY THE RECORD CANNOT SETTLE ARRIVAL AND DWELL. The fee stands or falls on POL-NS-01, whose four limbs the driver must carry together. Limbs (b) and (c) are read off the GPS trace EV-GPS-00901, and that trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08(b): issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6. Three inter-fix intervals inside the waiting window run 180, 240 and 180 seconds — each above the 120-second limb; the window from the 08:43 arrival marker to the 08:51 cancellation holds only four fixes against the six that limb requires; and the rider_track is omitted entirely. The trip record's 08:43 'arrived' marker is not a second source: the pre-pass records that it was auto-confirmed from that same GPS measurement, so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and the trace are one carrier, and the trace alone must prove the fact.

WHAT THE ARRIVAL TEST RETURNS. POL-NS-02 admits only fixes reporting horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better. No fix in this trace reports any accuracy figure at all, so no fix is admitted and the proximity test admitted no reading; the derived qualifying_fix_count is 0. That zero cannot be read as proof the driver never arrived, because POL-NS-02 itself says a trace too sparse to establish three consecutive in-radius readings is 'impaired under POL-NS-08(b) rather than proof of absence'. Limbs (b) and (c) are therefore UNDECIDED over the only stretch that matters: the record neither puts the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD radius for the 300-second minimum nor shows him absent from it. An undecided limb supports neither the full refund the rider seeks nor the fee the driver seeks.

THE DRIVER'S CHAT-LOG ARGUMENT. I considered the argument that EV-CHAT-00901, a complete artifact at weight 1.0, cleanly corroborates 480 seconds of waiting. I accept the log as evidence that the driver was messaging through the window, but it does not carry the fact the clause decides on: POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-02 measure arrival and dwell from the gps_trace, not from the chat, and a party's own account of his own arrival records only that he said it. Where the test admitted no reading at all, an account offered in its place is standing in for the test; it neither lifts the confidence cap nor stops the impaired trace from being the only evidence of arrival and dwell. The rider's mirror-image argument fails the other way: under POL-NS-04(c) an absent rider track is neutral, and the rider-presence test simply could not be run.

WHY ESCALATION. All of the evidence for the deciding fact — arrival and dwell — is the impaired trace. POL-NS-08 directs that where the only evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under its limbs (a) to (d), the case escalates under POL-NS-09, and POL-NS-09(e) is squarely engaged. Independently, the deciding fact is carried only by an artifact at weight 0.6, below the policy's 0.70 confidence floor, which engages POL-NS-09(a); my confidence is capped at 0.6 accordingly.

THE FARE LINE — A SEPARATE, REAL DEFECT. Both sides rightly flag that EV-FARE-00901 is impaired (PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.75) and that its $5.00 cancellation line does not reconcile with the fee schedule: the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00) is $4.00, a difference of $1.00, which engages POL-NS-08(d). I record that defect. Because the fee is held rather than refunded, no money moves on it now, but the reviewer must settle both the chargeability of the fee and, if it is chargeable, the fact that it cannot stand above the $4.00 the schedule authorises. The same impairment does not let the driver's compensation be paid, because POL-NS-01 is not carried in full.

WHAT THE REVIEWER MUST SETTLE. The open question is the driver's arrival and dwell on evidence measurable under POL-NS-02 — whether he was inside the 50 m STANDARD radius at or before 08:43:00 and held there for 300 continuous seconds. The escalation packet carries both advocate briefs, the admissibility pre-pass report, the clause IDs relied on (POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-04, POL-NS-05, POL-NS-06, POL-NS-08, POL-NS-09, POL-GEN-02) and this reasoning.

ON THE REMAINING CLAIMS. The driver's POL-NS-05 point is accepted: the 08:43 marker is not shown to be false, so no false-arrival referral issues. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip on driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d, and no lifetime counter (prior_no_show_flags) has been substituted for it, per POL-GEN-01; no profile field carries any adverse finding here. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider — she sent no locating message and the driver both replied and placed a call — but that clause is not what decides this case. No clause in the policy produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty.

Limbs (a) and (d) are satisfied on the platform's own trip record (EV-TRIP-00901, weight 1.0): it carries an 'arrived' event at 08:43:00 and a driver termination at 08:51:00 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event. The charge therefore turns on limbs (b) and (c) — that the driver's GPS placed him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and held there for the 300-second minimum dwell.

Both of those limbs read the driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00901, weight 0.6), and that trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08(b): five inter-fix intervals exceed 120 seconds (180, 240, 180, 180, 180 s), the waiting window from 08:43:00 to 08:51:00 holds only four fixes where the limb requires six, and the trace omits the rider track. It is also accuracy-blind — no fix reports horizontal accuracy — so POL-NS-02's proximity test, which admits only fixes accurate to 25 m or better, admits nothing at all. qualifying_fix_count is 0 and no in-geofence dwell can be computed.

Because the trip record's 08:43:00 marker was auto-confirmed from the same GPS measurement, the marker and the trace are one carrier, not two. Arrival and dwell therefore rest on a single artifact of weight 0.6, below the platform's 0.70 floor. POL-NS-08's final sentence and POL-NS-09(e) require escalation where the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b); POL-NS-09(a) requires it independently because the confidence cap is 0.6.

Rider (R-7823). Your principal arguments are not accepted as grounds for a refund. POL-NS-02's own drafting note says a trace too sparse to establish three consecutive in-radius readings is impaired under POL-NS-08(b) rather than proof of absence, and a limb whose instrument is impaired is undecided: it supports neither the fee nor a refund. So the zero qualifying-fix count is not evidence the driver was absent, just as it is not evidence he was present, and your POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 claims (the 300-second shortfall) establish the impairment rather than the refund. Your point is nevertheless preserved in this way: the no-show case against you has not been made out on this record, which is why the $5.00 is held rather than collected.

Driver (D-2398). Limbs (a) and (d) of POL-NS-01 are accepted. POL-NS-05 is correctly not engaged: the pre-pass finds no clock skew, and the trace shows a minimum distance of 0 m to the pin, so the arrival marker is not shown to be false. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider — the chat log (EV-CHAT-00901) contains no rider message, and you both replied in chat and placed in-app call CALL-00901-001 — but that clause is not what decides the case. Your claim that the chat log independently corroborates a 480-second wait is not accepted: the chat log records your own messages, and no clause reads the chat log as the test for the arrival or dwell limbs. Removing the impaired trace, the chat log would not by itself establish arrival, so it does not lift the 0.6 cap. Your POL-NS-07 compensation claim (the derived figure of $4.00, 80 percent of the itemised fee) does not arise, because compensation is payable only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and it is not. The anti-farming check neither trips nor clears you: no_show_terminations_30d is null, and POL-GEN-01 correctly bars substituting the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter for it.

Fare defect. Independently of the GPS dispute, the fare ledger (EV-FARE-00901, weight 0.75, PARTIAL_RECORD) charges $5.00 when the fee schedule produces $4.00 — the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00). That is a POL-NS-08(d) mismatch. It cannot be monetised now that the case is escalated, but it is recorded in the escalation packet.

Open questions for the reviewer. (1) Did the driver actually arrive at the pickup pin and hold there for 300 seconds? The trace cannot settle it; a re-pull of the GPS data carrying accuracy figures, or the driver's registered location at the arrival marker, would. (2) Whether the $1.00 charged above the $4.00 schedule fee should be refunded regardless of how the arrival question is resolved.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you have raised fair points, and the record cannot settle the one question this dispute turns on. I am sending the case to a human reviewer and holding the $5.00 cancellation fee rather than collecting or refunding it.

What is agreed. The platform trip record (EV-TRIP-00901) shows a driver 'arrived' event at 08:43:00 for TRIP-2026-09945 and a driver-side cancellation at 08:51:00 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00901) holds six entries between 08:43:00 and 08:51:00 — four driver messages and the system cancellation notice; the rider sent none.

Why I cannot rule on the fee. Under POL-NS-01 a no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions hold. Limb (a) (an 'arrived' event) and limb (d) (termination on one of the three recognised codes) are met. Limbs (b) and (c) are read from the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00901), and that trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08(b): five of its seven inter-fix intervals exceed 120 seconds (180, 240, 180, 180 and 180 s), the eight-minute waiting window holds only four fixes where that limb requires six, and it carries no rider track. No fix reports horizontal accuracy, so none can pass POL-NS-02's 25 m filter and the derived qualifying in-radius fix count is 0. That zero is a gap in the measurement, not a measurement of absence: POL-NS-02 says a trace too sparse to run its proximity test is impaired rather than proof the driver never arrived, and fixes without accuracy count as evidence of neither presence nor absence. So limbs (b) and (c) are undecided, not failed, and an undecided limb supports neither the fee nor a refund.

Why this escalates. The deciding fact — whether the driver arrived and held the pickup geofence for the required 300 seconds — rests on the GPS trace alone at weight 0.6. The trip record's 08:43 marker was auto-confirmed from the same GPS measurement, so marker and trace are one carrier, not two independent ones, and chat messages are not the test POL-NS-01 reads for arrival or dwell. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence on the deciding fact is therefore capped at 0.6, below the platform floor of 0.70. Under POL-NS-08 the ruling may not exceed PARTIAL_REFUND where the only evidence for the deciding fact is impaired, and under POL-NS-09(e) and (a) the case goes to a human reviewer. The $5.00 is held: not collected, not refunded, pending review.

Rider. Your POL-NS-02 argument (no qualifying fix means the driver never arrived, so full refund) is a fair reading of the clause's bare words, but it is displaced by the impairment that produces the zero — the count is zero because no fix carries accuracy, not because the fixes place the driver away from the pin. Your POL-NS-06 shortfall argument stands in the same position: the 300-second shortfall and the 0.0 s dwell are computed off the impaired trace, so they cannot carry a refund on their own. Your fare observation is sound and I record it for the reviewer: the ledger (EV-FARE-00901) charges a $5.00 cancellation line while the fee schedule yields $4.00 (the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee of $4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of $4.00) — a $1.00 discrepancy that engages POL-NS-08(d), on a ledger that is itself impaired (PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.75). Because chargeability as a whole is going to review, I hold the entire $5.00 rather than refunding the $1.00 in isolation.

Driver. Your POL-NS-04 points are accepted: the rider sent no message, so limb (a) fails, and you both replied in chat and placed an in-app call (CALL-00901-001 at 08:47:05), so limb (b) fails too; that clause exonerates no one here. You are also right that POL-NS-05 does not catch your arrival marker — the trace cannot place you more than 300 m from the pin or above 15 km/h at 08:43:00, and it records a minimum distance of 0 m. But none of that establishes a chargeable fee, because limbs (b) and (c) remain undecided on the impaired trace, and your chat-log timing (08:43:00 to 08:50:45, about 480 seconds) is not the measurement POL-NS-01(c) reads — that clause measures dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from messages. Your POL-NS-07 compensation claim cannot issue either: the anti-farming check does not trip because driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is null, not '4 or more', so on a chargeable fee you would receive 80% of the itemised fee, but the fee's chargeability is precisely what is undecided and escalation holds the money. The profile fields on both sides are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carry no finding.

Open question for the reviewer. Whether the driver in fact arrived and held the pickup geofence for the required 300 seconds, to be settled from an accuracy-bearing GPS record or another artifact that can stand as that test; and, if the fee is found chargeable, the $1.00 reconciliation between the $5.00 ledger line and the $4.00 schedule figure. No referral is issued, because no clause on these facts directs one.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-02 makes arrival an arithmetic question, and the arithmetic fails for the driver. The STANDARD-zone arrival radius is 50 m and the proximity test admits only fixes reporting horizontal accuracy of 25 m or better. Not one of the eight fixes in the driver's trace carries an accuracy figure, so under POL-NS-02 every one of them is ignored for this test and counts as evidence of neither presence nor absence. The derived arrival block records qualifying_fix_count = 0, rider_qualifying_fix_count = 0 and longest_qualifying_run.fix_count = 0 across the whole trace. POL-NS-02 states in terms that where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee. The trace is impaired at weight 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, and I disclose that impairment; it only weakens the trace as proof of arrival and cannot supply the arrival the driver needs, because the driver bears the burden of all four conjunctive limbs of POL-NS-01 and has not carried limb (b).

Independently of arrival, the waiting period the fee is meant to purchase never happened. The STANDARD minimum dwell is 300 seconds. The derived arrival block records longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec = 0.0, accumulated_dwell.longest_run_sec = 0.0 and accumulated_dwell.run_count = 0, against a shortfall_sec of 300.0. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full on a shortfall, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, so limb (c) of POL-NS-01 fails. And because no qualifying dwell ever elapsed, the 08:51 termination cannot satisfy limb (d) either: that limb requires the trip to end at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, and there was no such moment. These figures come from the impaired trace (weight 0.6; LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD), which I disclose; a record whose sampling gaps run to 240 seconds cannot be read as a continuous five-minute hold.

The driver cannot repair the shortfall by accumulating separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i). That limb requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, whose geometry covers the pickup road and whose active window covers the waiting period, carrying a type of KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. The only advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00901-01, is MISSING: weight 0.0 and no payload. Limb (i) is therefore unavailable and no interval may be summed. The absence is itself citable — there is no advisory on this record that could have made holding position at the pin lawfully impossible — and the 300-second minimum stands unadjusted.

ledger.claim: The GPS trace is impaired for policy purposes, not merely tagged. Five of the seven inter-fix intervals exceed POL-NS-08(b)'s 120-second gap limb (180, 240, 180, 180 and 180 seconds), the waiting window from the 08:43 arrival marker to the 08:51 cancellation holds only four fixes where that limb requires six, and the trace omits the rider_track entirely. Each of those is limb (b) on its own. The trace's weight is 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, and I disclose that any claim of mine resting on it is down-weighted; the consequence for this case is that no uninterrupted 300-second in-geofence hold can be evidenced at all, so the fee has nothing behind it.

The ledger does not reconcile with the policy that fixes the amount. POL-NS-01 fixes the chargeable fee at the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), which is $4.00, and POL-NS-08(d) makes a mismatch between fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee and that figure a fare defect. The ledger charges $5.00, a difference of $1.00. The artifact is impaired at weight 0.75 with issue code PARTIAL_RECORD, which I disclose. Whatever else is decided, no ruling can leave the rider paying $1.00 more than the schedule authorises, and this defect is independent of the GPS dispute — it is a defect on the platform's own ledger line.

The facts that decide this dispute — the driver's arrival and his dwell — are carried by a single carrier. The trip_record's 08:43 marker was auto-confirmed from the same GPS measurement, so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and the trace are one artifact and not two, and no independent artifact corroborates either fact. POL-GEN-02 caps confidence at the weight of the artifact carrying the deciding fact, which here is 0.6, below the 0.70 floor. On this record the pipeline cannot sustain a charge against the rider, and to the extent the judge finds the deciding fact rests solely on impaired evidence, POL-NS-09(a) and (e) require the case to escalate with the disputed $5.00 held rather than collected — which at the very least means the rider does not fund a charge the record cannot support.

ledger.claim: POL-NS-04 is the rider's principal route to a no-fault refund on coordination grounds, and its limb (a) fails outright. Limb (a) requires at least one message from the RIDER during the waiting window whose content is locating or coordinating — their own position, an entrance, block, tower or bay identifier, a request for the driver's position, or a statement that they cannot see the vehicle. The chat log runs from 08:43:00 to 08:51:00 and holds six entries; every one is from the DRIVER or the SYSTEM. The rider never asked where the car was, never named an entrance or bay, and never said they could not find the vehicle. Limb (a) is not met, so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider.

Even if limb (a) were somehow met, POL-NS-04 limb (b) is affirmatively failed. The clause requires that the driver NEITHER replied in the chat within 120 seconds of the rider's message NOR placed an in-app voice call before terminating. The driver did both. He posted messages at 08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30 and 08:50:45, and the trip record carries in-app call CALL-00901-001, initiated by the DRIVER at 08:47:05 and unanswered after 22 seconds. On either limb the rider-exonerating clause does not apply and no refund flows from it.

POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are satisfied on the platform's own records. Limb (a): the trip record contains a driver 'arrived' event for this trip at 08:43:00, auto-confirmed from a GPS measurement. Limb (d): there is no boarding event, the trip status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER, and it terminated at 08:51:00 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes limb (d) recognises. The rider-displacing clauses POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 do not fire (argued below), so the fee stands as itemised.

The dwell limb is corroborated by a clean artifact independent of the GPS. The chat log, at weight 1.0, shows the driver present and waiting from his 08:43:00 message — 'I've arrived at the pickup point, I'm at the lobby area' — through his 08:50:45 message — 'Please let me know, otherwise I'll have to cancel the trip' — with intermediate messages at 08:45:20 and 08:49:30 identifying the vehicle (white Honda HR-V, SGP 4521 M). That is 480 seconds of continuous presence at the pickup, comfortably above the 300-second STANDARD minimum, closing only when the SYSTEM logs the cancellation at 08:51:00.

I disclose that the GPS trace on which the rider's arithmetic must rest is IMPAIRED: issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, weight_multiplier 0.6. Five of its seven inter-fix intervals (180, 240, 180, 120, 120, 180, 180 seconds) exceed POL-NS-08(b)'s 120-second gap limb, the waiting window holds only four fixes against the six that limb requires, and no rider track was supplied. Under POL-GEN-02(1) that impairment must be stated in the same claim that cites it, and under POL-NS-08 a claim resting on this artifact is down-weighted: it cannot alone support a ruling against the driver.

The rider's cleanest arithmetic route is POL-NS-02, but the clause cannot carry it here. POL-NS-02's own drafting note states that a trace too sparse to establish three consecutive in-radius readings is 'impaired under POL-NS-08(b) rather than proof of absence'. This trace is exactly that shape — four fixes inside the waiting window, with no accuracy data. The absence of a qualifying in-radius fix is an impairment of the record, not a demonstration that the driver never arrived, and the clause's stated consequence (limb (b) fails, full refund) does not attach to a trace the clause itself classifies as impaired. (The trace is impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

POL-NS-02 admits only fixes whose reported horizontal accuracy is 25 m or better, and not one fix in this trace reports any accuracy field at all. The derived qualifying_fix_count of 0 therefore measures the trace's missing data, not the driver's conduct: on its own terms the clause's proximity test cannot be run, and the policy itself says such fixes 'count as evidence of neither presence nor absence'. The zero dwell figure cannot be turned into an affirmative finding against the fee. (The trace is impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

POL-NS-05 sets aside an arrival marker only where the trace places the driver more than 300 m from the pin at the marker, or shows him travelling at 15 km/h or above. Neither is established here. The pre-pass records no clock skew — the 08:43:00 marker is the nearest fix timestamp to the second, so POL-NS-08(a) is not engaged — and the driver's own track records a minimum distance to the pickup pin of 0 m across its fixes, with a mean of 274 m and a maximum of 1,109 m, the profile of a vehicle that drove up to the pin and held there. The marker is not false on this record and the waiting clock runs from it. (That derived minimum is drawn from the impaired trace: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

POL-NS-06 refunds a rider only where the effective in-geofence dwell, computed under POL-NS-02, falls short of the minimum for the zone class. No such dwell is computable here, because no fix carries the accuracy POL-NS-02 requires, so the clause's premise cannot be established on this record. Its accumulation limb (i) is expressly unavailable as well: EV-ADVIS-00901-01, the traffic advisory, is MISSING, and limb (i) requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated. A MISSING artifact keeps its identifier, carries weight 0.0, and can carry no fact; it cannot be asserted against, and it exonerates no one. The shortfall arithmetic therefore proves nothing against the fee. (The GPS trace is impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

ledger.claim: If the Judge concludes the record cannot settle arrival and dwell, the disposition that protects the fee is escalation, not refund. The trip record's auto-arrival marker and the GPS trace's zero qualifying fixes contradict each other directly on arrival and on dwell, and no clause resolves that conflict because the trace is accuracy-blind — POL-NS-09(b). In the alternative, the sole evidence for the deciding dwell fact is the trace, impaired under POL-NS-08(b), which caps the ruling at PARTIAL_REFUND and sends the case to the human reviewer under POL-NS-09. On either path the disputed fee is held rather than refunded while review is pending. (The trace is impaired: LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.6.)

I disclose a further defect rather than leave it to my opponent: the fare ledger is IMPAIRED — issue code PARTIAL_RECORD, weight_multiplier 0.75 — and its SGD 5.00 cancellation line does not reconcile with the fee schedule, which yields SGD 4.00 as the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00). That mismatch engages POL-NS-08(d). It is a defect in the amount recorded, not in the chargeability of the fee: it cannot convert a legitimate no-show charge into the full reversal the rider seeks.
